output.brief:
The slowdown comes from one change. Credit Policy v14, effective 1 May, now requires a full inspection appraisal for property-secured loans between $150k and $500k. Before, those loans got a quick desktop valuation. Full appraisals take about 8.6 days, against 1.2 days for desktop. The valuation stage for property-secured loans rose from about 1.6 days to 8.4 days. Orders in that band carry the policy code from 2 May. The firm's turnaround hasn't changed, and its contract renewal isn't the cause. Unsecured loans are back near their March times. Corvane is therefore not the cause, and neither are the new hires: document collection at their branches matches the others. Staffing and volume at the Credit Hub don't explain it either, because underwriting time is flat. The policy change was never assessed for its effect on processing times. The policy's reason is an audit finding that desktop valuations ran about 12% high.

Next steps: don't withhold the Corvane payment, and don't put the new hires on improvement plans. Take the measured delay and the audit rationale to the credit risk committee and ask it to decide on the $150k–$500k rule. Add a by-stage timing view to the dashboard. I'm unsure whether longer waits cause the extra withdrawals. The 30-day auto-close rule may also inflate them. Check that before offering any customer incentive. Confidence is high on the main cause.
